Also, to approve the trading margin of Rs. 0.07/kWh to be charged from the DISCOM(s)/Buying Entity(ies) on the sale of power as specified in the RfS document and specified in the Guidelines. [¶] - iii. The Petitioner further contrasted the discovered tariff with the NVVN standalone BESS tender (250 MW / 1000 MWh), which discovered a tariff of ₹6.64/kWh on 28.07.2025. The Petitioner emphasized a crucial differentiator: while the NVVN tender benefited from Viability Gap Funding (VGF) support (up to ₹27 lakh/MWh or 30% of capital cost), the FDRE-4 projects receive no VGF subsidy. The Petitioner stated that despite the absence of any subsidy and the stringent requirement [¶] - (a) Addressing the Commission’s query regarding the delay in filing the adoption petition, the Petitioner submitted that following the issuance of Letters of Award (LoAs) on 10.11.2025, it undertook necessary steps to engage with various Buying Entities/DISCOMs for the procurement of power. Given the novel nature of the scheme (Assured Peak Power coupled with Energy Storage Systems), the Petitioner required additional time to ascertain the Buying Entities' willingness and to facilitate the execution of downstream arrangements, such as Power Sale Agreements (PSAs). Furthermore, the Petitioner submitted that time was also expended in achieving tariff uniformity, as two of the successful bidders voluntarily agreed to match the L1 tariff of ₹6.74/kWh in late November 2025. The Petitioner asserted that the Petition was ultimately filed on 26.12.2025 only after the completion of these essential processes. Asserting that the delay was occasioned by the bona fide and unavoidable additional time required to secure procurement consents and facilitate downstream contractual arrangements integral to the scheme's implementation, the Petitioner prayed for the condonation of the delay.
